findings.r3_note: The en-dash check was extended beyond em dashes because the project's rule covers both, and the R1 file-level check would not have caught the real exposure. Measured: no prose file in final/ contains either character after R3 edits, but 13 of the 41 ledger entries carry an em or en dash INSIDE their exact_passage. These are source text inside verbatim quotations, from the GENIUS statute text (SS-010 through SS-013), the IMF working papers (SS-020, SS-022), the Kansas City Fed capture (SS-102), the BCG and Allium white paper (SS-030, SS-031) and aggregator captures (SS-070, SS-072, SS-073, SS-090). They are left intact deliberately: replacing them would break the verbatim match that verify_captures.py enforces, and a source quote is the one place where the project's typography rule cannot outrank fidelity. The rule applies to authored prose. Where the synthesis itself needed a range outside a quotation it uses hyphens, for example '$350-$550 billion' in section 1.7.

r3_own_findings.title: The capture text extractor could silently delete evidence, and it had already hidden a real figure
r3_own_findings.measured_finding: final/evidence/build_claims.py stripped markup with the greedy pattern r"<[^>]+>", which treats a literal '<' in body prose as a tag opener. Measured on the stored captures by re-running both the legacy and the fixed normaliser over the same source text: a Spark Money table cell beginning '<$' swallowed 3,716 characters of real text (legacy flat 18,408 chars against fixed 22,124), including the BUIDL 'As of May 2026, BUIDL holds approximately $2.4 billion' sentence; an IMF WP/26/44 significance marker '<0' swallowed 26,586 characters (legacy flat 40,460 against fixed 67,046).
r3_own_findings.why_it_matters: A passage that the extractor deleted could never be found by the anchor, so the absence of a match looked like the absence of evidence. In this record that had a concrete cost: the May 2026 BUIDL figure, which the upstream causal-laguna ledger had already flagged as conflicting with the $2.5-2.9bn range, was invisible in the primary capture itself until the extractor was fixed. The verifier could not have caught this, because it verifies that a sliced passage exists in a capture, not that the capture extraction was complete.
r3_own_findings.fix: TAG_RE is now name-anchored (r"</?[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9:_-]*(?:\s[^<>]*?)?/?>") and script/style bodies are dropped before tags are stripped. The legacy normaliser is retained as flat_legacy() so the defect stays reproducible on demand.
r3_own_findings.post_fix_check: All 41 passages re-sliced from source; 41/41 SLICED_VERBATIM. build_claims.py re-run twice, claims.json and evidence-manifest.json byte-identical both times.
r3_own_findings.carried_into_prose: final/synthesis.md section 8 records the defect with the measured character counts, so a reader can see that the evidence chain itself was audited and not merely the quotations.

r3_own_findings.title: The x402 volume floor of $996 thousand was never sourced to any capture, and has been withdrawn
r3_own_findings.measured_finding: final/synthesis.md quoted a bottom of range of '$996 thousand' across 18.1 million transactions. No capture in the record contains either number. The real x402scan page capture (final/evidence/x402scan.html) was never copied into final/evidence/, and its global totals live inside the page's embedded RSC payload in <script> tags, which the markup stripper removes, so no claim could previously rest on it.
r3_own_findings.why_it_matters: This is the pattern the record already flags elsewhere: a headline figure paired with a computed ratio or a range endpoint that no source made. It was the bottom of an x402 range that section 1.6 builds on.
r3_own_findings.fix: build_claims.py gained extract_x402scan(), one explicit regex over the captured payload, which writes final/evidence/x402scan.html.txt containing the verbatim totals plus a tool unit conversion; it raises rather than degrades if the payload is absent. New claim SS-085 carries 12,293,450 transactions, 27,467 buyers, 38,519 sellers and 974,215,144,043 raw USDC units ($974,215.14 at six decimals, mean $0.079247 per transaction, both tool-computed). The $996 thousand figure is withdrawn and recorded as excluded in section 7.
r3_own_findings.carried_into_prose: final/synthesis.md section 1.6 now gives the evidenced low point, names the withdrawal, and states that the dashboard's window and inclusion rules are not stated in the capture, so its total still cannot share an axis with an August-only five-chain count.

r3_own_findings.title: The x402 bot-attribution rested on one firm; two independent corroborations were added from captures already in the record
r3_own_findings.measured_finding: Section 1.6 previously offered Bitquery's 83 percent two-loop finding with no independent corroboration inside the same sentence structure. Two relevant captures were present in the record and unused: the Chainalysis adoption post and the Visa and Artemis agentic-payments note.
r3_own_findings.why_it_matters: The section's central claim is that a large, independently measured share of x402 activity is automated. That word 'independently' needs more than one firm behind it, and SS-082's own uncertainty field already conceded the gap.
r3_own_findings.fix: SS-083 (Chainalysis: growth driven substantially by meme coin farming, PING pay-to-mint at 1 USDC, over 150,000 transactions in its first month) and SS-084 (Visa and Artemis: about $15.0 million adjusted volume across 109.6 million transactions since the May 2025 launch, wash and test activity excluded) added, both sliced verbatim. Section 1.6 now separates the corroboration from the Bitquery attribution and states that SS-084 is scoped differently (wash-adjusted, single ecosystem, as of April 2026) and does not average with the cross-chain counts.
r3_own_findings.honest_limit: SS-084's value and transaction count sit far apart, which is consistent with the section's argument, but it is a different measurement of a different ecosystem and is not offered as a substitute for the Bitquery volume. The true commerce share of x402 volume remains UNRESOLVED and no source in this record estimates it.
